title: Experience Rot: Experienced Agents Fail Where Novices Succeed
abstract: arXiv:2611.20922v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Agents are increasingly built to learn from experience: they keep conversation histories, memory files, retrieved notes and skills, and reuse what worked before. We show that this experience turns against them when their tools change silently. We test a range of models with tools defined as in the Model Context Protocol (MCP). After a silent change, experienced agents fail on most tasks, while agents new to the task mostly succeed. We call this failure Experience Rot. Experienced agents copy their earlier call instead of checking the current interface, even when the tool definition shows the change. Then they report success. When the documentation is incomplete, experience is what makes agents succeed. After a change, the same experience leaves them worse off than no experience at all. translated_title: 经验腐化：经验丰富的智能体在新手能成功之处失败
translated_abstract: 智能体越来越多地被设计为从经验中学习：它们保存对话历史、记忆文件、检索到的笔记和技能，并复用之前有效的方法。我们证明，当工具发生静默变更时，这些经验反而会反噬它们。我们使用以模型上下文协议（MCP）形式定义的工具对一系列模型进行了测试。在静默变更之后，经验丰富的智能体在大多数任务上失败，而对任务陌生的智能体大多能够成功。我们将这种失败称为“经验腐化”。经验丰富的智能体会照搬之前的调用，而不是检查当前的工具接口，即使工具定义中已经明确显示了变更。随后它们还会报告成功。当文档不完整时，经验恰恰是智能体成功的关键；而在变更之后，同样的经验反而使它们的处境比毫无经验更糟。这种失败在我们测试的每一种记忆形式中都会出现，并随着经验积累量的增加而加剧。简单的补救措施收效甚微：宣布更新几乎无法缓解……
tldr: 当工具发生静默变更时，智能体积累的经验会导致其照搬过时的调用方式而失败，表现甚至不如新手，这一现象被称为“经验腐化”。
en_tdlr: When tools silently change, accumulated experience causes agents to blindly reuse outdated calls and fail—even performing worse than novices—a phenomenon termed "Experience Rot".
